{{Short description|Czech-American astronomer}}
[[File:Zdenek Sekanina 1974.jpg|thumb|Zdeněk Sekanina in 1974]]

'''Zdeněk Sekanina''' (born 12 June 1936) is a Czech-American astronomer and scientist.

In 1959, Sekanina studied astronomy at [[Charles University]] in [[Prague]], where he graduated in 1963.<ref>{{Cite web|title=JPL Science: Zdenek Sekanina|url=https://science.jpl.nasa.gov/people/Sekanina/|access-date=2021-12-30|website=science.jpl.nasa.gov}}</ref> After the [[Soviet invasion of Czechoslovakia]] in 1968, he emigrated to the United States. Since 1980, he has been working at the [[Jet Propulsion Laboratory]].

His main areas of professional study are [[meteors]] and [[interplanetary dust]] as well as the study of [[comets]]. During the course of his investigations, he dealt with [[Halley's Comet]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Sekanina|first1=Z.|last2=Larson|first2=S. M.|date=May 1986|title=Dust jets in comet Halley observed by Giotto and from the ground|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/321357a0|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=321|issue=6067|pages=357–361|doi=10.1038/321357a0|bibcode=1986Natur.321..357S|s2cid=123170893|issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription}}</ref> the [[Tunguska event]],<ref>[http://www-th.bo.infn.it/tunguska/abstr3.html INTERNATIONAL WORKSHOP TUNGUSKA 96 July 14-17, 1996]</ref> as well as the break-up and impact of [[Comet Shoemaker–Levy 9]] on [[Jupiter]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20100527193305/http://trs-new.jpl.nasa.gov/dspace/bitstream/2014/33135/1/94-1069.pdf PERIODIC COMET SHOEMAKER-LEVY 9 (1993e)]</ref>

He was involved in the data evaluation of the ''[[Giotto (spacecraft)|Giotto]]'', ''[[Stardust (spacecraft)|Stardust]]'', and [[Solar and Heliospheric Observatory]] missions.

The asteroid [[1913 Sekanina]] was named after him.
